concept.title: Activate the shell honestly
paragraphs: Earlier scaffolding created a non-buildable Web folder shell containing architecture-preview folders and .gitkeep files. It did not contain a Web project file, Program.cs, or solution entry. Session 33 preserves that shell and activates it with the official .NET Web template.

Structural CLI operations make cause and effect visible: dotnet new creates a project, dotnet add reference creates a dependency, and dotnet sln add changes solution membership. Inspect the resulting files after each operation.

concept.title: Transport contracts are not Domain objects
paragraphs: ClockInRequest and ClockEntryResponse are small HTTP data carriers. Positional records concisely create constructors and properties and provide value-based equality. Sealed says these exact shapes are not inheritance bases.

Records do not validate input, protect Domain invariants, replace Domain objects, or guarantee every possible form is immutable. Separate request and response types may evolve independently even when their properties currently match. One important public type per matching file is this repository's discovery convention, not a C# requirement.

concept.title: Read the action result from the inside out
paragraphs: ClockEntryResponse is the successful response-body shape. ActionResult<ClockEntryResponse> can represent that value or another HTTP ActionResult. Task<ActionResult<ClockEntryResponse>> means that HTTP outcome becomes available asynchronously.
BadRequest selects HTTP 400, Conflict selects HTTP 409, and Created selects HTTP 201. The helper selects the protocol status; its message is only response content.

concept.title: Program.cs is the composition root
paragraphs: Program.cs connects concrete pieces without taking over their responsibilities. Remember: register, build, initialize, map, run.

Registration stores the recipe. Resolution creates the object. The scope owns the context; the database outlives both. AddControllers prepares controller services; MapControllers exposes controller routes.

lab.title: Activate the Web shell and expose clock-in
lab.objective: Create and run POST /clock-entries/clock-in over the existing async application and persistence boundaries.
lab.task: Activate the existing Web shell, implement one clock-in controller action, compose its dependency graph, and verify real HTTP behavior.
lab.startingCondition: Earlier scaffolding created a non-buildable Web folder shell with placeholder folders but no .csproj, Program.cs, or solution entry. Preserve those folders while activating the shell.

steps.text: Inspect src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Web before generating anything. Confirm the placeholder folders exist and that the shell has no Web .csproj or Program.cs. Do not delete placeholders and do not use --force. After this step, 23 numbered steps remain.
steps.code: find src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Web -maxdepth 2 -type f -print | sort
steps.completeWhen: The existing shell has been inspected and its buildable versus placeholder state is known.
steps.purposeAfter: The course acknowledges earlier work instead of pretending the Web area never existed.

steps.text: Define readable Bash variables for the repeated solution and project paths. Braces in ${project_prefix}.Web mark where the variable name ends before .Web is appended. After this step, 22 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
project_prefix="PinkMachine19.TimeClock"
web_project_name="${project_prefix}.Web"
web_directory="src/$web_project_name"
web_project_file="$web_directory/$web_project_name.csproj"
domain_project_file="src/${project_prefix}.Domain/${project_prefix}.Domain.csproj"
infrastructure_project_file="src/${project_prefix}.Infrastructure/${project_prefix}.Infrastructure.csproj"
solution_file="${project_prefix}.sln"
steps.completeWhen: All seven descriptive variables print or expand to the intended paths.

steps.text: Run the official Web template in the inspected shell. --framework is one option token; standalone -- would instead end option parsing. The template creates the Web SDK project, minimal Program.cs, settings, launch profile, and restore-ready structure. If those files already exist correctly from an earlier attempt, inspect them and continue rather than overwriting. After this step, 21 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
dotnet new web \
  --name "$web_project_name" \
  --output "$web_directory" \
  --framework net10.0
steps.completeWhen: The shell contains a net10.0 Web SDK .csproj and a non-empty minimal Program.cs.

steps.text: Add explicit references from Web to Domain and Infrastructure. Domain exposes the application contracts and service types used at the HTTP boundary; Infrastructure supplies EF Core persistence types and implementation. After this step, 20 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
dotnet add "$web_project_file" reference "$domain_project_file"
dotnet add "$web_project_file" reference "$infrastructure_project_file"

dotnet list "$web_project_file" reference
steps.completeWhen: The reference listing shows Domain and Infrastructure exactly once.

steps.text: Add the Web project to the solution, then inspect solution membership. dotnet sln add changes solution membership; it does not create the project. After this step, 19 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
dotnet sln "$solution_file" add "$web_project_file"
dotnet sln "$solution_file" list
steps.completeWhen: The Web .csproj appears in the solution listing.

steps.text: In Requests/ClockInRequest.cs, use the comment-first scaffold to type a public sealed positional record with int EmployeeId and DateTime ClockInTime. A record fits this small named transport value set and supplies value equality; sealed prevents inheritance. It does not validate input or protect Domain invariants. Keep this important public contract in its matching file for discovery and independent evolution. After this step, 18 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: ClockInRequest.cs contains the learner-authored record declaration beneath the comments.

steps.text: In Responses/ClockEntryResponse.cs, type the corresponding public sealed positional response record using the comment-first scaffold. Keep it separate because incoming and outgoing HTTP contracts may evolve independently even when today's properties match. C# permits multiple types per file; this is a repository convention, not a language rule. After this step, 17 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: ClockEntryResponse.cs contains the learner-authored response record beneath the comments.

steps.text: Create the Controllers folder if absent, then create ClockEntriesController.cs. Paste the using and framework shell. ApiController enables API conventions; Route establishes the base path; ControllerBase supplies HTTP helpers without MVC views; sealed prevents inheritance but does not make the class static. After this step, 16 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: The controller file contains the attributes and empty ControllerBase-derived shell.

steps.text: Add constructor injection inside the controller. The controller translates HTTP; AsyncClockEntryService coordinates the use case. Declare the explicit private readonly field, receive the concrete service, and assign it. Program.cs will provide it later. After this step, 15 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: The controller stores its injected AsyncClockEntryService in _service.
steps.purposeAfter: HTTP translation depends on the use-case coordinator without constructing persistence itself.

steps.text: Read the return contract inside out: ClockEntryResponse is the success body; ActionResult<ClockEntryResponse> permits that value or another HTTP result; Task<ActionResult<ClockEntryResponse>> makes the outcome asynchronous. Paste the action attribute and signature, but leave behavior as comments for yourself to implement. After this step, 14 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: The action shell compiles conceptually as the intended nested contract and the body contains only guidance comments.

steps.text: Implement the validation branch. Choose the protocol result first: BadRequest returns HTTP 400 regardless of its message. Expand the conversion once with explicit types: BadRequest returns BadRequestObjectResult, which inherits from ActionResult; ActionResult<ClockEntryResponse> can wrap that result. ASP.NET Core defines the types and conversion, the compiler enforces it, the IDE displays analysis, and async machinery creates the outer Task. After this step, 13 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: A non-positive EmployeeId returns a visibly constructed HTTP 400 outcome.

questionsAfter.question: Why can this return without constructing ClockEntryResponse?
questionsAfter.answer: ClockEntryResponse is the success-body path. ActionResult<ClockEntryResponse> can instead hold an ActionResult such as BadRequestObjectResult.

questionsAfter.question: Am I returning a Task directly?
questionsAfter.answer: No. Inside an async method, the return expression supplies ActionResult<ClockEntryResponse>; compiler-generated async machinery completes the outer Task.

steps.text: Implement the awaited service call with an explicitly typed bool named accepted. Pass request.EmployeeId, request.ClockInTime, and the same cancellationToken. This forwards request cancellation to genuine asynchronous database work. After this step, 12 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: The action awaits the service once and visibly forwards cancellationToken.

steps.text: Implement the false branch with Conflict. Conflict selects HTTP 409; writing the word Conflict inside BadRequest would still produce 400. Choose the helper from protocol meaning, then write useful content. After this step, 11 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
// If accepted is false, return Conflict with a message
// explaining that an open clock entry already exists.
steps.completeWhen: The false service outcome returns Conflict rather than BadRequest.

steps.text: Create the successful response and location with explicit types. The $ enables string interpolation and braces identify the inserted C# expression. Then pass both variables to Created, which selects HTTP 201. Inline construction is only a later concise equivalent. After this step, 10 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: The success path returns HTTP 201 with an explicit response object and interpolated location.
steps.purposeAfter: The action now follows validate → await service → forward cancellation → inspect accepted → translate to HTTP.

steps.text: Before editing Program.cs, read the two lifecycle maps. Program.cs is the composition root: it connects concrete pieces without taking over their jobs. After this step, 9 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
create builder
→ register every service
→ build provider/application
→ create startup scope
→ resolve actual DbContext
→ ensure database schema
→ dispose startup scope/context
→ map controller routes
→ run host

HTTP request scope
→ ClockEntriesController
→ AsyncClockEntryService
→ IAsyncClockEntryRepository / EfClockEntryRepository
→ TimeClockDbContext
→ SQLite
steps.completeWhen: You can state which graph exists at startup and which graph is created per HTTP request.
steps.purposeAfter: The remaining framework calls now have an ordering and ownership model rather than appearing as unrelated boilerplate.

steps.text: Replace the generated Program.cs only within that file, preserving a recoverable editor history. Begin with the EF Core using, create an explicitly typed WebApplicationBuilder, and call AddControllers before Build. AddControllers registers services needed to construct and execute controllers. After this step, 8 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: Program.cs is saved, non-empty, and contains builder creation followed by AddControllers before any Build call.

steps.text: Expose EF configuration before inference compresses it. Create an explicitly typed Action<DbContextOptionsBuilder> delegate whose typed parameter calls UseSqlite with Data Source=timeclock.db, then pass it to AddDbContext<TimeClockDbContext>. The selected overload expects this delegate, which is why the compiler can infer the shorter lambda later. Registration without UseSqlite may compile but fails when database work begins. After this step, 7 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: The DbContext recipe visibly includes the SQLite provider and connection string before Build.

questionsAfter.question: Did AddDbContext create the startup context?
questionsAfter.answer: No. It registered a construction recipe and scoped lifetime. Resolution creates an instance later.

questionsAfter.question: Who infers an untyped lambda parameter in the shorter form?
questionsAfter.answer: The C# compiler applies the selected overload's Action<DbContextOptionsBuilder> contract. The IDE only displays language analysis.

steps.text: Register IAsyncClockEntryRepository to EfClockEntryRepository and register AsyncClockEntryService, both scoped, using explicit generic calls. Scoped matches one graph per HTTP request. After this step, 6 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: Every constructor dependency for ClockEntriesController has a registration before Build.

steps.text: Build the WebApplication only after AddControllers, AddDbContext, and both AddScoped registrations. builder.Services is mutable registration state; Build creates and finalizes the provider. Remember register → build → initialize → map → run. After this step, 5 numbered steps remain.
steps.code: WebApplication app = builder.Build();
steps.completeWhen: Exactly one builder.Build call appears after every registration and before startup initialization.

steps.text: Add a bounded startup scope. Registration stores the recipe; resolution creates the object. CreateScope provides a legitimate scoped boundary before any request, GetRequiredService constructs the configured context, and EnsureCreatedAsync creates the schema when absent. Leaving the braces disposes the startup scope, context, tracking state, and temporary resources—not timeclock.db, its schema, or saved data. After this step, 4 numbered steps remain.
steps.completeWhen: The initialization scope ends before route mapping and app.Run; the scope owns the context and the database outlives both.
steps.purposeAfter: Startup uses a real configured context without extending its scoped lifetime until host shutdown.

steps.text: Map controller routes, then run the host. AddControllers prepared controller services; MapControllers reads route attributes and exposes endpoints. Route clock-entries plus HttpPost clock-in produces POST /clock-entries/clock-in. app.Run must be last. After this step, 3 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
app.MapControllers();

app.Run();
steps.completeWhen: Program.cs ends with MapControllers followed by app.Run and contains no generated root MapGet.

steps.text: Save and inspect Program.cs before building. If a top-level Web project reports CS5001, first verify Program.cs exists, is non-empty, and contains top-level statements; use editor undo or local history instead of destructive recovery. Build Web in Release from current source. After this step, 2 numbered steps remain.
steps.code: dotnet build "$web_project_file" --configuration Release
steps.completeWhen: The saved, non-empty Web project builds in Release with zero errors.

steps.text: Start the freshly built Web project and note its actual listening base URL. EnsureCreatedAsync must succeed and the host must report that it is listening. GET / may return 404 because the only endpoint is POST /clock-entries/clock-in; a browser address bar sends GET. After this step, 1 numbered step remains.
steps.code:
dotnet run --project "$web_project_file" --configuration Release --no-build

# In another terminal, substitute the actual listening URL:
curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:5000/clock-entries/clock-in" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"employeeId":0,"clockInTime":"2026-08-18T09:00:00"}'
steps.completeWhen: The host listens and the invalid POST returns HTTP 400; an optional valid POST returns 201 and an immediate repeat returns 409.

steps.text: Stop the host, then build the complete Release solution and run the complete suite with --no-build. --no-build runs existing compiled output, so it is trustworthy only after the matching build. Open Solution Reveal only after these checks. After this step, 0 numbered steps remain.
steps.code:
dotnet build "$solution_file" --configuration Release
dotnet test "$solution_file" --configuration Release --no-build
steps.completeWhen: The complete Release solution builds and every test passes.
steps.purposeAfter: Session 33 has proven the Web project, HTTP translation, cancellation forwarding, dependency graph, SQLite startup, and repository-wide compatibility.

lab.expectedBehavior: POST /clock-entries/clock-in returns 400 for a non-positive employee ID, 409 when an open entry already exists, and 201 with ClockEntryResponse after successful persistence.
lab.validation:
dotnet build src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Web/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Web.csproj --configuration Release
dotnet run --project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Web/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Web.csproj --configuration Release --no-build
dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release
dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

commit: session-33: add the async clock-in api
review: The existing placeholder Web shell is described truthfully and preserved.
The official Web template creates routine host files.
Domain and Infrastructure references are both verified.
Request and response contracts remain separate from Domain and persistence types.
The controller selects 400, 409, and 201 through the correct helpers.
All registrations and SQLite configuration precede Build.
The startup scope ends before MapControllers and Run.
The freshly built host starts before full-solution validation.

postQuiz.prompt: What determines whether the response is HTTP 400 or 409?
What does AddDbContext do before any resolution?
options: Registers a construction recipe and scoped lifetime
Creates the SQLite file without a context
postQuiz.explanation: Registration stores the recipe; resolution creates the object.

postQuiz.prompt: Why can GET / return 404 while the application is healthy?
postQuiz.explanation: Routing matches both HTTP method and path.

reflections: Which responsibilities belong to the controller rather than the service?
Which objects end when the startup scope closes, and what persists?
Where does compiler inference shorten a type relationship that was shown explicitly first?
whatBreaks: Removing the Web project leaves the shell non-buildable. Incorrect result helpers change the HTTP contract. Registrations after Build or missing UseSqlite fail at startup. An unbounded startup scope keeps its DbContext alive until host shutdown.
summary: Session 33 activates the existing Web shell, exposes one deliberate async clock-in endpoint, and proves the complete HTTP-to-SQLite composition.
